name: Sclerotinia Leaf Rot
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves Leaves turning yellow and wilting Soft rot on infected leaf tissue White cotton-like fungal growth on leaves or stems Black seed-like sclerotia forming in infected areas Leaves collapsing and dying
description: Sclerotinia leaf rot is a fungal disease that affects many crops. The fungus infects leaves and stems under cool and wet conditions. It produces white cotton-like mold and black survival structures called sclerotia.
management: Remove infected plants quickly Improve plant spacing and airflow Rotate crops with non-host plants Remove infected plant debris from fields
prevention: Avoid overcrowded planting Monitor crops during cool and wet seasons Practice crop rotation Use integrated disease management
